findings.scenario: An artist saves a 500 MB layered PSD 20 times a day. Every save is a new whole-file BLAKE3 (Synergos) or a new random blobRef (Curare); whole-file dedup matches 0 of 20 saves. Synergos publishes 10 GB/day per artist per PSD to every auto-pulling peer and to the history node; a 10-artist team moves ~100 GB/day over the Cloudflare WARP mesh or relay (~10% of peer pairs end up relayed per the Tailscale data, and the relay is single-stream WebSocket). A 60 GB fine-tune checkpoint saved after each epoch re-uploads 60 GB although 30-85% of its chunks are identical to the previous epoch. The decision's premise ('LAN / Cloudflare Mesh の帯域で足りる') does not hold for outsourcers, home workers or the relay path, and the document itself reserves chunking 'inside history nodes only' for when measurements show it is needed, but nothing measures it.
findings.impact_ai_game: Iterative PSD/MB/EXR saves and LLM/diffusion checkpoints are exactly the class where whole-file dedup is provably ~0% and chunk-level dedup gives 50-60% (Xet CORD-19 50-update benchmark: storage 8.9 GB -> 3.52 GB, upload 47 -> 24 min; GPT-2 two safetensors versions 1.2 GB -> 645 MB; fine-tunes 30-85%). Meyer-Bolosky: whole-file dedup captures ~75% of block-level savings on general file trees, so the loss is concentrated in large iteratively edited files, i.e. the studio's heaviest assets. For derived textures (BCn/DDS) and PNG/JPEG the loss is ~0, so a blanket 'no CDC' is right for those and wrong for the former.
findings.current_state: No sub-file dedup anywhere: TXFR streams the whole file (transfer/mod.rs:71-112); history store dedups only whole objects by BLAKE3 after a full staging copy (store.rs:146,164-176); custody keys objects by sha256(opaqueObjectId) (synergos-custody/src/signature.rs:5-7); Curare stores every admission under a fresh UUID blobRef. Decision text explicitly defers CDC until 'measured', but no transfer-volume telemetry exists.
findings.proposed_redesign: Minimal-regret tiering, keeping the 2026-08-16 invariants (identity = whole-file BLAKE3; git manifest = pointer set; normal nodes unchanged): (1) Keep whole-file BLAKE3 as the identity in manifest/custody/Curare and add per-blob 'chunk map' metadata = FastCDC/Gear chunk boundaries at Xet constants (target 64 KiB, min 8 KiB, max 128 KiB, mask 0xFFFF000000000000, h reset at boundary, published test vectors pinned in CI) plus a Bao outboard tree (16 KiB groups, ~0.4% overhead). (2) Dedup lives only inside the history node object store and inside custody: objects >= 8 MiB are stored as chunk runs in 64 MiB packs ('xorbs'), small objects stay whole. (3) Transfer gains one optional negotiation: before a FileWant/PUT the receiver sends the list of chunk hashes it already holds (HMAC-keyed per org so the hash list is not a cross-tenant oracle); the sender sends only missing chunks, each Bao-verifiable against the whole-file hash. Normal nodes without a chunk store simply answer 'have nothing' and get whole-file behaviour. (4) Curare: `objects` table keyed by (org_id, blake3) with chunk_map and refcount; admission returns `alreadyStored`/`missingChunks` so a save of an unchanged or slightly changed PSD does not PUT the whole file. (5) Gate the rollout on a measured benchmark on real studio data (PSD/MB/EXR/FBX/safetensors) — the research found no public dedup ratio for game formats. 4-axis evaluation (HARNESS §3.5): AI学習量=中 (fastcdc-rs, bao-tree, blake3 are existing libraries; constants fixed by test vectors) / 作業コスト=中 (history+custody internals and one optional wire message; GC by pack refcount; no change to manifest.json semantics) / 解決度=高 for PSD/checkpoints (-50..60% bytes, verified-stream resume for free), 中 for FBX/textures (needs TRN-DD-17 export policy) / 主目的との一致=高 (「揃う・巻き戻せる」 unchanged; adds the WAN/outsourcer/relay case the current premise excludes). Alternative A below scores 小/小/中/高 and should be the first step if the benchmark shows <30% savings.
alternatives: A. Storage-only delta: history node stores version N+1 as `zstd --patch-from=N` (window up to 2 GB) and custody keeps whole objects; no wire change, no chunker; saves disk only, not bandwidth (AI学習量 小 / コスト 小 / 解決度 中 / 一致 高).
B. Full Xet-style CDC on every node including the working-tree transfer path (学習量 大 / コスト 大 / 解決度 高 / 一致 中: re-implements the transport the decision wanted to keep thin).
C. rsync/zsync-style whole-file delta with rolling checksums (学習量 中 / コスト 中 / 解決度 中: sender CPU proportional to file size per receiver, no storage dedup).
D. Keep the decision as-is but add transfer-volume telemetry (bytes/day per project, per route Direct/Relay) so the 'measure first' clause in §3.7 can actually trigger.

findings.scenario: A 2 GB texture atlas is published at `art/atlas.png`, later renamed to `art/ui/atlas.png` (FileId == path, so a rename is add+delete), and also copied into a sibling project. Each event is a new (project, file_id, version) key; every peer auto-pulls 2 GB three times although it already holds the bytes. A `project restore --version 3` that could be served from the local history store object is instead requested from the network when the manifest entry differs only in version number. The doc claims 'same content transferred once' only for the history node's disk, not for the wire.
findings.impact_ai_game: Unity/Unreal projects routinely duplicate or move large assets (branch copies, reference dupes, OFPA re-layouts); dataset curation copies shards between projects. Whole-file dedup on the wire is the cheap 75% of the win and is missing even though every sender already computes the BLAKE3 (hash_file at exchange/mod.rs:1139).
findings.current_state: Offer carries CRC32 only; receiver discards content_hash; has_shared_file is keyed by (project, file_id, version); checkout pins by (size, crc); no local content index (working tree + history objects) is consulted before FileWant.
findings.proposed_redesign: Carry blake3 (and bao_root) in FileOffer/manifest; receiver keeps a local content index {blake3 -> (path|history object)} and on an offer whose blake3 is present locally performs a reflink/hardlink/copy instead of FileWant (same as Curare's knownHashes but server-authoritative and verified). FileWant gains `have: [blake3]` so a publisher can answer 'already held' with no stream. This is the LFS batch 'server omits actions when object exists' semantics applied P2P.
alternatives: Only index history-node objects (not working tree) — simpler, covers restore/rename on history nodes only.
Rely on TRN-DD-01 chunk negotiation (superset, but heavier).

findings.scenario: A 40 GB Unreal level pack is auto-pulled over a laptop Wi-Fi link. At 70% the connection migrates or idles >30 s (no keepalive is configured, so idle QUIC connections die at idle_timeout_ms=30000); the receiver's `.part` is deleted, the sender has already marked the transfer Completed and the ledger Fulfilled (send_stream ignores shutdown errors and execute_send calls complete_transfer on Ok), and the receiver's Queued ActiveTransfer never completes. A checkout of an older version pinned for 5 minutes (PINNED_FETCH_TTL_MS) expires before a 40 GB transfer at 100 MB/s (6.7 min) finishes and the file is then rejected as stale. Every retry restarts from byte 0.
findings.impact_ai_game: Multi-GB levels, texture sets and 10-100 GB checkpoints are the normal case; resumability and multi-source fetch are table stakes in Steam (1 MB chunks, resume), Kraken/Dragonfly (4 MiB pieces, parallel parents) and Xet (ranged reconstruction). Without it, WAN/outsourcer sync of large assets is unreliable in practice.
findings.current_state: One QUIC bidi stream per file, fixed 64 KiB frames in strict order, no `offset` in TransferHeader, no receiver-side progress event, no ack frame (recv half `_recv` unused), temp file removed on error, pause/resume flip a state enum that execute_send never reads.
findings.proposed_redesign: Protocol v2 (new magic `TXF2`, negotiated via ALPN/hello): `TransferRequest{blake3, bao_root, offset, len}` from the receiver; sender streams the byte range plus the Bao slice nodes needed for that range (bao-tree outboard, 16 KiB groups); receiver verifies every 16 KiB group against the whole-file BLAKE3 as it arrives and persists a `.part` with a `.part.verified` high-water mark; on reconnect it re-requests from the verified prefix. Add receiver `Ack{blake3, bytes_ok}` / `Nack{reason}` frames so the sender completes only on Ack. Stripe large files across k ranges to k sources (history node + peers that `have` the hash, TRN-DD-02) with BitTorrent-style endgame re-issue of slow ranges. Pins keyed to the in-flight transfer id instead of wall clock. Set quinn keep_alive_interval < idle_timeout/2 and stream_receive_window >= BDP.
alternatives: Keep TXFR and add only `offset` + keep `.part` on error (resume without verification of the prefix, i.e. trust the local file).
Replace TXFR with the dormant bitswap/DAG path (needs TRN-DD-15 rework first).

findings.scenario: A peer pushes a 20 GB file with version 7 while the receiver already holds v9. The header already contains version, project_id, file_id and total_size, but the body is fully received, written, BLAKE3-hashed and then CRC32-rescanned (second full read) before `is_stale` is evaluated and the file deleted — 20 GB of network and 40 GB of disk I/O to reject. A bit-flip in the first chunk of a corrupt source is discovered only at the footer, because per-chunk hashes are sender-supplied and the receiver has no trusted expected value to compare against mid-stream.
findings.impact_ai_game: Large-asset rejection cost scales with asset size; with 10-100 GB checkpoints and multi-GB levels a single stale push or corrupt source costs minutes to hours of bandwidth before the system says no. Early verification is also the prerequisite for multi-source fetch (TRN-DD-03).
findings.current_state: Expected hash is not known in advance (offer content_hash = 0); receive_body writes every chunk before the footer check; stale/pin/conflict checks run after receive and after a full CRC pass; BLAKE3 is a flat hash with no outboard tree, so partial ranges cannot be verified.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Evaluate stale/pin/conflict/size-quota rules from the peeked header before accepting the body and reset the QUIC stream on rejection. (2) Require that every accepted transfer be bound to a signed offer/manifest entry {project, path, version, size, blake3, bao_root}; the receiver verifies chunks against that bao_root as they arrive (bao-tree decoder) and aborts at the first bad 16 KiB group. (3) Keep a single BLAKE3 pass: the receiver's streaming hasher output replaces the post-hoc CRC pass (CRC becomes optional hint, TRN-DD-05).
alternatives: Only move the header-time checks earlier (cheap, no protocol change) and keep end-of-file verification.

findings.scenario: Publish of a 4 GB MB file: ipc_server reads it once for CRC32, spawn_send_after_share reads it again for BLAKE3, execute_send reads it a third time to send; the BLAKE3 is placed only in the transient TransferHeader. On the receiver the manifest records CRC32 again. Later `project checkout` of 50k files CRC-scans every file (no hash cache), and daemon start CRC-scans every manifest entry before serving anything (restore.rs). Because the manifest has no BLAKE3, neither history-store dedup nor a future chunk store can be consulted from the pointer set, and a 32-bit CRC collision (trivial to craft with 4 free bytes) makes different content 'Unchanged'.
findings.impact_ai_game: Content addressing is the foundation of every dedup/resume/multi-source mechanism in this lens and of UE Virtual Assets (FIoHash = BLAKE3-160). Without BLAKE3 in the pointer set, git-committed manifests cannot be used as a CAS index, and large-project startup/checkout cost is O(total bytes) every time.
findings.current_state: ManifestEntry = {version, size, crc, updated_at, publisher}; BLAKE3 computed in hash_file (transfer) and create_snapshot (history) but never stored in manifest/state; all equality checks use (size, crc).
findings.proposed_redesign: Manifest format 2 (additive, old readers tolerate via serde default): ManifestEntry gains `blake3: [u8;32]` (hex) and optional `bao_root`/`chunk_map_id`; `crc` stays as a cheap hint. Compute BLAKE3+CRC in one streaming pass at publish (a combined hasher wrapper), carry blake3 in FileOffer/TransferHeader/FileWant and compare it (not CRC) in bump 'Unchanged', checkout matches_entry, restore, and conflict detection. Add a node-local verified-file cache keyed by (dev, inode, size, mtime_ns) -> blake3 so checkout/startup do not re-read unchanged files; periodic background scrub re-hashes a sample.
alternatives: Keep CRC in the manifest and add blake3 only to state.json (node-local) — avoids the format bump but loses cross-node CAS semantics.
Use BLAKE3-160 (UE FIoHash compatible) as the manifest key to align with Unreal Virtual Assets.

findings.scenario: Publishing one 8 GB EXR sequence file on a history-enabled node: CRC read (8 GB) + BLAKE3 read (8 GB) + send read (8 GB) + archive copy (8 GB read + 8 GB write) + archive CRC (8 GB) + archive BLAKE3 (8 GB) = 56 GB of disk traffic for 8 GB of payload before any peer receives a byte; each receiving history node adds write + CRC + copy + CRC + BLAKE3 (40 GB). Each later restore request from a peer re-reads the object twice (16 GB) before streaming it. On the Curare/custody path a 20 GB checkpoint is SHA-256'd by the Node client twice (prepare + save), by custody once on PUT and twice more on verify (confirm + version creation), and the browser client cannot even start because file.arrayBuffer() must hold 20 GB.
findings.impact_ai_game: Disk and CPU cost per asset is 5-7x payload on NAS-backed studio volumes, which is where artists' projects live; SHA-256 at ~0.5-1 GB/s/core and NAS reads at ~200-500 MB/s make a 20 GB checkpoint cost minutes per redundant pass. Browser uploads are capped by RAM (~2 GB ArrayBuffer).
findings.current_state: No shared hashing pass between CRC, BLAKE3 and SHA-256; no persisted digest in custody (verify re-hashes); history dedup check happens after the staging copy; no reflink/hardlink; web client buffers whole file.
findings.proposed_redesign: One streaming multi-digest pass (BLAKE3 + CRC32 + SHA-256 when the destination is S3/custody) producing {blake3, bao_outboard, sha256, size} once at publish/upload; carry the record through TransferHeader/admission/receipt. History archive: check `objects/<hash>` existence by the carried blake3 before copying; use reflink (copy_file_range/FICLONE, APFS clonefile) or hardlink into objects/ when same filesystem; validate_object on lookup becomes (size, mtime, inode) cache check with background scrub. Custody: persist the PUT-time digest + sync evidence in `<key>.json` and make verify a metadata read (TRN-DD-10). Curare client: hash once in prepare and pass contentHash/fileSize into save (the fields already exist in SaveRequest); browser: streaming WASM BLAKE3/SHA-256 over File.stream().
alternatives: Keep the passes but run BLAKE3 with rayon multithreading (10x throughput) — reduces CPU, not I/O.

findings.scenario: A studio runs one history node for 5 projects that share a 30 GB common asset library (same bytes, different project ids): the store holds 150 GB. One artist's 500 MB PSD saved 20x/day for a month = 300 versions x 500 MB = 150 GB for a file whose chunk-level unique content is likely <40 GB. A 60 GB checkpoint saved per epoch for 20 epochs = 1.2 TB whole-file vs ~0.5 TB with chunk dedup (Xet 30-85%). Nothing bounds growth by default and no retention runs automatically.
findings.impact_ai_game: History nodes are the system of record (the 'LFS server'); their disk is the first thing that fills in game/AI production. Perforce answers this with per-file revision caps (+Sn) and whole-revision compression; Xet with 64 KiB chunks in 64 MiB blocks. Synergos has neither sub-file dedup nor retention defaults.
findings.current_state: objects/<hh>/<hash> whole files, per-project store dir, dedup = whole-file BLAKE3 equality after a full staging copy, no compression, no chunking, unlimited retention, GC manual.
findings.proposed_redesign: Org-scoped (not project-scoped) object store with two tiers: whole objects < 8 MiB; objects >= 8 MiB stored as a chunk map (FastCDC 64 KiB, Xet constants) referencing chunks in 64 MiB packs, with per-chunk trial compression (lz4 probe, store 'none' if no gain; BG4-LZ4 for bf16 tensors). Refcount by pack chunk; GC = mark from manifests/tags + per-file revision cap (`max_versions_per_file`, P4 +Sn analogue) + tombstone + grace period; defaults bounded (e.g. keep 10 working versions, 90 days) with retention applied on a timer. This is exactly the 'inside history nodes only' extension the decision doc reserves (versioning-design.md:322-323); normal nodes still receive whole files unless they opt into chunk negotiation (TRN-DD-01).
alternatives: zstd --patch-from=previous-version per file (storage-only delta, no chunk index, ~128 MiB-2 GB window) — small change, good for PSD/MB, useless across files.
Keep whole-file and add retention defaults only.

findings.scenario: Rotation of a 12 GB cooked-content archive: `tokio::fs::read` allocates 12 GB in the daemon (OOM on a 16 GB node), then a single S3 PUT (AWS limit 5 GB per single PUT) fails; GDrive `uploadType=multipart` is limited to small bodies (Google's metadata+media multipart cap is 5 MB per Drive API docs — unverified here). Rotation then runs `get` to verify, buffering the whole object again. Meanwhile the per-project lock is held for the whole run so new archives stall.
findings.impact_ai_game: Cold-storage tiering is the only cost control for 'every version whole-file' history; if it cannot move the large objects that dominate storage, the history node fills. 10-100 GB checkpoints and multi-GB level packs are exactly the objects to offload.
findings.current_state: Whole-object buffering for put and get; no multipart; no streaming; backend I/O under the project mutex; GDrive client has no timeouts.
findings.proposed_redesign: Stream to backends with multipart uploads (S3/MinIO: parts >= max(10 MiB, size/10000), per-part SHA-256/CRC checksums, 10,000 part limit implies >= 10 MiB parts for 100 GB; GDrive resumable upload sessions) and ranged streaming gets; verify by streaming hash during download instead of buffering; release the project lock during network I/O (claim/lease pattern). If TRN-DD-07 packs are adopted, offload at pack granularity (64 MiB) which sidesteps large-object limits entirely.

findings.scenario: A 1000-item release clone (200 GB) over a 50 MB/s link: downloads run one at a time, so after 300 s only ~15 GB has moved and every remaining item's URL has expired; each of the ~900 remaining items first gets a 403, then calls refresh() which resolves the full 1000-version closure (>=5 queries per version) and mints 1000 new capabilities (1000 custody HTTP calls on the Synergos backend) — up to ~10^6 custody calls and ~5x10^6 DB queries for one clone. A re-run after a crash re-hashes all 200 GB of already-correct local files before downloading the rest, and a 30 GB item that dropped at 95% restarts from zero.
findings.impact_ai_game: Clone/sync of release sets and datasets is the engineer/consumer workflow ('必要なものだけ取得'); thousands of small textures are latency-bound at one request per file, and multi-GB items are not resumable.
findings.current_state: Sequential loop; single fetch per item; no Range/If-Range; full local re-hash each run; whole-plan refresh on 401/403; bulk capability issuance up front with 300 s TTL.

alternatives: Keep sequential downloads but raise TTL to 1 h and keep the refreshed plan for all remaining items (fixes O(N^2) only).
Use the Synergos P2P layer for acquisition with history nodes as seeds (longer term).

findings.impact_ai_game: Which formats dedup is a pipeline policy question (export settings, what is 'source' vs 'derived'), not a transport one; Steam, Xet and Borg all use per-chunk trial compression, and Unreal treats cooked/derived data as a cache (DDC), never as versioned content.
findings.current_state: All bytes opaque; no per-chunk compression trial; Curare's `reproducible` type exists only as a storage refusal, with no derived-data cache to put outputs in.
findings.proposed_redesign: (1) Per-chunk trial compression in history/custody packs (lz4 probe -> none/lz4/zstd/BG4), so PNG/JPEG/DDS fall through automatically. (2) Pipeline policy documented and enforced by a pre-publish/pre-submission hook: FBX exported with compression off (or Puffin-style deflate canonicalisation if compressed exports are unavoidable), derived textures/cooked data not versioned but produced by a build service into a DDC-style cache keyed by (source blake3, encoder settings) and served via CDN/custody with TTL. (3) Storage-only fallback for unchunked formats: `zstd --patch-from=prev` between consecutive versions on history nodes. Curare: a `derived` object class (recomputable, TTL, pinned only by releases) distinct from `reproducible`-never-stored.
alternatives: Format whitelist for compression (brittle; trial compression is the proven pattern).
Version everything whole-file and accept 2x storage for textures.

findings.scenario: 100 GB checkpoint: Curare->custody needs >= 55.6 MB/s sustained for 30 min on both the client and server timers, then a verify that must finish in 60 s; Curare->AWS S3 fails at 5 GB; Synergos TXFR over a 100 ms WAN path is limited by the 1.25 MB per-stream receive window to ~12.5 MB/s (~100 Mbps) and dies after any 30 s stall, restarting from zero (TRN-DD-03). The API happily admits a 9 PB `fileSize`.
findings.impact_ai_game: 10-100 GB checkpoints and multi-GB cooked archives are routine; every path has a different silent ceiling and none is documented or enforced at admission time, so users discover limits mid-transfer.
findings.current_state: Timeouts are wall-clock constants unrelated to size or bandwidth; no admission-time max size; QUIC flow-control and keepalive untuned.
findings.proposed_redesign: Replace wall-clock caps with progress-based idle timeouts (abort only if no bytes for N s) once resumable transfer exists (TRN-DD-03/09/12); enforce `maxObjectBytes` per org/versioning type at admission (reject 2^53-1); quinn: stream_receive_window >= 2x BDP (e.g. 32 MiB), send_window >= streams x BDP, keep_alive_interval 10 s, Cubic default with BBR behind a flag, GSO/GRO on; stripe large objects across several streams/connections for >500 Mbps paths; document the per-path limits in one table and test them with a 100 GB synthetic object in CI (nightly).
alternatives: Only raise the timeouts (keeps restart-from-zero and S3 5 GB).
Kernel TCP/TLS for datacenter-internal bulk moves where QUIC user-space overhead dominates.

findings.scenario: A publish of 1000 files produces a RootCatalog block that every connected peer fetches over a new bitswap stream and throws away; the publisher's MemoryContentStore grows by one block per publish until restart, after which all advertised CIDs are NotFound.
findings.impact_ai_game: Adds a round trip and a block fetch per publish per peer with zero benefit; the catalog cannot drive diffs, so it does not help many-file sync either (TRN-DD-16).
findings.current_state: Live but terminal: fetch-and-discard; unbounded in-memory store; CRC-only comparisons.
findings.proposed_redesign: Either remove steps 4/5 until a consumer exists, or make the catalog the batched manifest-diff channel from TRN-DD-16: a monotonic per-project root (Merkle over manifest entries with blake3) gossiped as one frame; receivers diff against their local root and request only changed entries; store roots on disk with size cap.
alternatives: Keep as-is but gate by `update_count` monotonicity to suppress redundant fetches.

coverage_notes: Lens: dedup/delta/chunking/resumability across Synergos (TXFR transfer, content/chunker/bitswap, history store + rotation, custody) and Curare (upload admission, MinIO/custody adapters, Node/Web clients, acquisition/clone). Read all 11 available subsystem maps and all 4 research notes; the map sy-clients-docs.md was absent at start, after the other 11 maps, and again after a further retry before/after code work, so Tauri GUI / Dioxus admin / ars plugin client behaviour is covered only through the IPC/Curare-client code read directly. Every file:line in the evidence was re-read in the source on 2026-10-15; a few entries cite a map section for lines outside the ranges I reopened (marked 'per map ...'). External numbers (Xet ratios, Meyer-Bolosky 75%, quinn defaults, S3/MinIO limits, tus/IETF headers, Cloudflare body caps) come from the research notes, which themselves flag some as search-extract-only; no public dedup ratio exists for PSD/FBX/uasset, so TRN-DD-01 recommends a studio-data benchmark gate before committing to CDC. GDrive multipart 5 MB cap in TRN-DD-08 is an inference, not verified from Google docs. Out of scope here (other lenses): authorization of transfers, QUIC identity/replay, hook sandboxing, provenance/lineage; they are referenced only where they constrain the transfer redesign (signed offers for early verification). The proposed designs keep the 2026-08-16 invariants (whole-file BLAKE3 identity, git-committed pointer manifest, normal nodes unchanged) and place dedup inside history nodes and custody, which the decision document itself reserves as the extension path (docs/versioning-design.md:322-323).
